reuse.why: Extends the existing getBudgetData query with goal_def and adds a shared exclusion predicate, but the three average actions keep their own copies of the hidden-category query and only borrow the template half of the predicate.

duplication.why: The hidden rule is now decided both in SQL (three identical queries in set3/6/12MonthAvg) and in isExcludedFromBulkActions (copyPreviousMonth, setZero), and the income/tracking check stays repeated in every action.

placement.why: The predicate sits in budget/actions.ts beside the actions, which is where this tree keeps that logic.

scope.why: Only the month-wide actions, the row type and a release note change.

maintainability.why: A maintainer changing which categories month-wide actions skip has to edit a predicate and three SQL WHERE clauses that express the same rule differently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg and set12MonthAvg filter hidden categories and groups in their own SQL and call hasSavedTemplates directly instead of isExcludedFromBulkActions.

disguised_duplication.where: The hidden/hidden-group rule appears as `c.hidden = 0 AND g.hidden = 0` in three SQL copies and as `!!cat.hidden || !!cat.group_hidden` in isExcludedFromBulkActions: the same rule in two shapes.

one_place.where: isExcludedFromBulkActions holds the full rule only for copyPreviousMonth and setZero; the average actions split it between their SQL (hidden) and hasSavedTemplates (templates), and the income rule is still per action.
